title: The Waiting Game: Pin the Pawn, Leave the Bishop a Move
summary: Avoid stalemate by leaving the bishop mobile, then remove the pinned pawn with a protected rook.

nodes.question: Why go to h8 instead of returning to the first rank?
nodes.explanation: Rh8 pins h2 against Kh1 while leaving Bg1 free to move. Rb1 would pin the bishop instead and stalemate Black. Nf3 protects h2 for the final rook capture.

branches.title: Source finish: allow the bishop to move
commentary: Begin after ...h2 in the complete saved 109-second eight-piece diagram. The earlier queen sacrifice and king walk are outside this proof.
Rh8 pins h2 against Kh1. The h-pawn cannot move onto its own king, g2 is blocked by Bg1, and the king has no square. Six bishop moves remain legal, so this is not stalemate.
Bf2 is the illustrated bishop move. It leaves h2 unprotected by the bishop; the other five legal bishop moves are included in the certificate.
Rxh2# removes the pawn with check. Nf3 protects Rh2 and controls g1; g2 is occupied by Black’s pawn. Black’s king cannot capture the rook or escape.
branches.explanation: Rxh2# removes the pawn with check. Nf3 protects Rh2 and controls g1; g2 is occupied by Black’s pawn. Black’s king cannot capture the rook or escape.

branches.title: Independent defense: move the bishop to a7
commentary: Compare the longest bishop retreat rather than assuming ...Bf2 is forced.
Rh8 creates the same pawn pin while keeping the bishop mobile.
Ba7 is legal, even though White’s king attacks that square. A bishop may move onto an attacked square; Black’s own king is not exposed.
Rxh2# still mates. The distant bishop cannot interpose against the adjacent rook check or capture Rh2.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Rxh2# still mates. The distant bishop cannot interpose against the adjacent rook check or capture Rh2.

exercises.answer: It pins Bg1 to Kh1. Both black pawns are blocked and the king has no square, so Black has no legal move and is not in check: stalemate. This contrast is separately checked by legal move generation.
Nf3 protects h2, preventing Kxh2, and also controls g1. The bishop has left g1, but that flight square is still covered.
